title: RDW–platelet coupling offers no reliable cross-cycle increment for ferritin prediction in nonanemic women
abstract: A single product of standardized red-cell distribution width (RDW) and platelet count was tested for incremental prediction of contemporaneous natural-log serum ferritin. A survey-weighted ridge model fitted to NHANES2005–2006 nonanemic, confirmed-nonpregnant women aged20–49 (n=904) was transferred without refitting to separately recruited NHANES2007–2008 women (n=905; actual eligible ages20–44). A flexible conventional baseline contained age, BMI, hemoglobin, mean corpuscular volume, RDW, red-cell count, platelet count, CRP and race/ethnicity. Target MSE was 0.535858 before and 0.535382 after adding the product: gain 0.000477 log² units, 0.089% relative reduction; joint source–target survey-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.011599, 0.010832]. Mean absolute error worsened. Source cross-validation and sensitivity analyses do not establish a reliable increment. This is a negative feature test, not proof that iron physiology lacks interactions or that ferritin testing can be replaced.
